steps.content: September, N.F. 74. DisCity completed its satellite town expansion, eliminating all opposition forces in the surrounding territories. The popularity and influence of Dravyn, the democratically elected Speaker of the City Council, reached its zenith.

As the glory of DisCity's independence burns bright, Speaker Dravyn leads our city-state to unprecedented heights! Now, we call upon our young warriors to secure vital resources and ensure stability and prosperity for all! Each mission is a sacred duty, a chance to demonstrate our strength and cement our city-state's future. Youth of DisCity, answer Speaker Dravyn's call! Take up the Reaper weapons, defend our honor with your passion, and ensure DisCity stands forever unconquered!

February, N.F. 78. To guard against counterattacks from metropole powers, DisCorps established a network of observation towers along the WhiteSands border. Equipped with the Reapers, these towers—dubbed "lighthouses" by other units—formed the Ash defense line. Their dual purpose was to monitor both the Tide of Ashes and Outland movements, while also serving as waypoints and supply stations for field squads.

June 15, N.F. 84, 14:29. The DisSea Explosion occurs, triggering global catastrophic anomalies. Border stations detect a "black tide" forming at the Operation Skyfall nuclear impact site, where contamination has merged with Mania mutations into a physical entity.

June 15, N.F. 84, 14:37. The Black Tide spreads at an alarming rate. Lighthouse OT-N02 organizes defensive perimeters and transmits distress signals to DisCity, requesting immediate reinforcements.

June 15, N.F. 84, 14:40. Communications are disrupted by BR-000 interference. OT-N02's distress signals receive no response.

June 15, N.F. 84, 14:42. The Black Tide's spread rate and intensity vastly exceed all known parameters of the normal Tide of Ashes. Mania contamination expands rapidly. Lighthouse OT-N05 is lost with all hands.

June 15, N.F. 84, 16:15. Surviving lighthouses, cut off from command, abandon their posts and begin independent evacuation procedures.

June 15, N.F. 84, 17:05. The evacuation failed. Lighthouse keepers are surrounded by the Black Tide. Only 50 survivors remain. With her final breath, OT-N07 Captain Fynn transmits a rallying signal, directing survivors to regroup at OT-N07 and continue sending SOS signals to DisCity.

December, N.F. 84. The lighthouse keeper unit is reduced to 23 survivors. All supplies are nearly exhausted.

March, N.F. 85. Only 12 people remain. Herbert assumes command after Captain Fynn's death and reorganizes the team. The unit has endured by discovering a pattern in the Black Tide: it recedes during daylight hours and becomes active at night, when Tide Crawlers emerge to raid the shore.

The stone slab at the base of the lighthouse is covered in tiny inscriptions. Weathered by wind, rain, and salt, the earliest markings have faded almost to nothing. As your gaze travels downward, the handwriting grows increasingly erratic, the style shifting so dramatically it suggests a different chronicler altogether.

December, N.F. 86. Herbert is gone. 11 lighthouse keepers remain. Scavenging for supplies grows more desperate. Mania contamination remains an inescapable threat.

April, N.F. 88. Miles discovered how to create edible food from the monsters.

February, N.F. 89. 8 lighthouse keepers remain.

May, N.F. 89. 3 remain.

November, N.F. 89. All are gone.

In this place, the high-concentration Mania had warped the fabric of space-time, rendering dates useless as anchors for record-keeping. After a long gap, the crude inscriptions resumed, now following a new format.

Suicide attempt #13. Lost consciousness, then woke up. Failed.
...
#506, or thereabouts. Lost count. Tried again. Left my Rancor behind and jumped into the Black Tide. Failed.
...
#2019. Survived again. Found someone from DisCity who crawled out of the Black Tide.

#2020. That DisCity person is still alive. The lighthouse went dark.
Not a flicker of emotion crosses her face as she carves what she knows will be the last inscription.

A lighthouse keeper must maintain the lighthouse. Must signal DisCity. Must always fight. The duties are etched into her memory. She knows she should climb to the lantern room and attempt a repair, but a strange inertia holds her fast. All she feels is a vague, gnawing irritation.
The tower clock ticks on, its chimes counting the hours for no one.
With sudden resolve, she spreads her arms and lies back in the sand. Squinting at the sky, she tries to quell the storm raging within her.
The sun has been a stranger here for years, its warmth a distant memory. The sea breeze is the only thing that touches her now, carrying the taste of salt across her cheeks.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: ...Maybe ending like this isn't so bad after all.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: At least I can finally get some peace and quiet.
<size=45>...Clink! Clank!</size> The jarring report of metal on metal shatters the silence.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Finally. Some. Peace. And. Quiet...
Ceto grits her teeth, forces a breath, and turns over. But then—CLANG CLANG CLANG CLANG!—the hammering escalates into a brutal percussion, a relentless pounding against the inside of her skull.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Tsk...
She clamps her hands over her ears, but the noise, sharpened by pure malice, drills straight into her mind.
<size=55>CLANG CLANG CLANG CLANG CLANG CLANG CLANG CLANG!</size>

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Stop it already!
At the other end of the beach, the "trouble" she'd scavenged from the shore is crouched over a pile of scrap. Hearing her, you look up.
Sorry for the noise. Just trying to get the lighthouse functional again.

Ceto's gaze sweeps over the heap of junk beside you: a tangle of broken pipes, bent valves, half of a signal device ripped from some forgotten machine. It looks as if an entire scrapyard has vomited its contents onto the sand.
Don't feel like you have to help. I can manage on my own.
Unless you'd prefer to lend a hand? We'd get off this island a lot faster if we worked together.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Who said I want to work with you...
She answers with a cold grunt, then turns away, lying back down to present you with her back.
Since last night, your invitation to leave together has been met with nothing but silence.
[Flashback] [Inside the Lighthouse]
I am the Chief of DisCity MBCC, an advisor to the Rancor squad, tasked with retrieving the remaining Rancors from the WhiteSands border.
Ceto froze for a moment, then slapped away your hand that was extended in an offer of alliance.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Hah. Here we go again. And what's your proof this time? That crumpled piece of paper in your pocket?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Last time, what was it? A merchant caravan? Looking for a friend? Well, congratulations on the new identity.
DisCity never abandoned you. The Rancor squad has been searching all this time. We risked approaching the Black Tide specifically to find border soldiers like you.
While you were stuck here, surrounded, something might be happening in the city, too. There had to be a reason they couldn't answer your calls.
And I'm sorry I lied about who I was. I didn't know if I could trust you. I had my reasons.
Causes, reasons, excuses... Ceto only responded with a cold, scornful laugh.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: You done?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: If you're done, then open your eyes and look around!
Ceto dragged you to the porthole and forcibly turned your chin toward the storm and monsters raging outside.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I let you poke around this island all day. Find anything to eat? Cook up a brilliant escape plan? You think you can survive that storm?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: You can't even save yourself, Mr. "Advisor"!
steps.female_content: You can't even save yourself, Ms. "Advisor"!

steps.content: There's still a chance. If we can just get the beacon working, send a signal...

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: A signal?!
She slams her fist into the wall.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: What do you think I've been doing for the last eight thousand days? Ringing a funeral bell for everyone under these waves? Is that it?
She leaned in, her breath a cold whisper against your ear, her face a mask of ice.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Keep your delusions to yourself. Don't you ******* drag me into them.
Without another word, she turned and retreated to the cabin's darkest corner, lying down and closing her eyes as if shutting a door.

Her outburst—the most words you'd ever heard her speak at once—left you speechless. You opened your mouth, but no sound came out. You had already seen the logs carved into the lighthouse wall, but at that time, the history of the old Rancors felt more impenetrable than ever.
I can't stand here and judge your past. What's done is done. But I can prove myself to you. No matter what it takes, I am getting off this rock and finishing what I need to do.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: It was a sacrifice. It was abandonment. A betrayal. The one thing it is not is the <color=#fb9259>past</color>.
...Help will come for us. I know it.
Your words hang in the air. A dead silence swallows the room, broken only by the eternal, hopeless sigh of the tide beyond the window.
If a miracle does happen... I'll ask you this question again: Will you leave this place with me?
[End of Flashback] [Beach, Daytime]
Irritating! That stupid question is as annoying as he is!
steps.female_content: Irritating! That stupid question is as annoying as she is!

steps.content: How can anyone be so naively certain of rescue? How can someone firmly believe they will reunite with their companions and work tirelessly toward that goal? Ceto cannot comprehend it. The very thought makes her feel as if sea urchins are crawling over her, their spines needling her skin. She shifts, but sleep remains impossible.
Even more grating is that persistent mumbling, buzzing like a mosquito that refuses to leave—
Checked the damage from last night after getting up. The monsters got the electrical circuits and the beacon housing, but the core light source is still intact. So we need power, and a new lens.
The radio's battery won't cut it for a bulb that big... Hydroelectric power? That's a massive project. We don't exactly have a hardware store lying around.
There must be some tools here for maintenance...

You deliberately draw out your words, testing for a reaction. As expected, Ceto isn't asleep. At the sound of your voice, she shifts slightly further away. Last night's tension clearly isn't dissipating.
No toolbox? Fine. I can make do with these cans. Where there's a will, right?
A wrench or a screwdriver... which first?
Ceto still shows no reaction, so you pick up an empty can with exaggerated deliberation.
Well, it's not like I have a choice. Unlike someone, I don't plan on turning into a salted fish on this island. So... time to start hammering!

options: I'm really going to start hammering now!

steps.content: [White Flash] [Hammering Sound]
Something flies through the air and knocks the can from your hand with a sharp clang.
It happened so fast that it takes you a moment to process what it is: a key.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: South shore. Cellar.
